name: Budapest
tagline: Thermal baths and a river of lights
summary: Spend one day on hilly Buda and one on flat Pest, with a long thermal soak in between. The Danube view after dark is the highlight, and it is free.
seasonNote: Summer is hot and festival-heavy; December brings Christmas markets.
arrival: The 100E express bus runs from the airport to the centre in about 40 minutes.
gettingAround: Metro, trams and buses share one ticket; tram 2 follows the river for the views.
cashTip: Pay in forints by card and decline conversion to your home currency; avoid Euronet ATMs.
foodTip: Try goulash soup, chicken paprikash, lángos and a chimney cake.
buyTip: Paprika, Tokaji wine and Herend or Zsolnay porcelain.
baseArea: District V, VI or VII in Pest

connections.note: Air time only; buses take about 7 hours.

items.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
items.summary: A vast neo-Gothic parliament on the Danube, with a gilded staircase and the Holy Crown.
items.expect: Guided tours only, and they sell out in summer.
items.tip: Book online ahead; see it lit up at night from the Buda bank.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.bestTime: Morning tour; evening from across the river

items.name: Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church

items.expect: Crowded from mid-morning; the upper turrets are ticketed in the daytime.
items.tip: Come at sunrise, when it is empty and free.

items.expect: A long walk across the hill; the funicular has queues.
items.tip: Walk up from the Chain Bridge or take bus 16.

items.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
items.summary: A yellow neo-baroque bath palace with large outdoor thermal pools open all year.
items.expect: Busy at weekends; bring flip-flops and a towel or rent them.
items.tip: Go on a weekday morning and book a cabin rather than a locker.
